title: Energy-aware Scheduling and Input Buffer Overflow Prevention for Energy-harvesting Systems
problem: Energy-harvesting IoT devices capture data at a fixed rate but process it at a dynamically varying rate determined by available ambient power; when capture rate exceeds processing rate the fixed-size input buffer overflows and events are permanently lost, and no existing dynamic solution prevents this across varying energy and workload conditions.
motivation: Missed events in energy-harvesting sensor systems (e.g., wildlife monitors, structural sensors) are unrecoverable, making input buffer overflow (IBO) prevention a hard correctness constraint that static scheduling and prior runtime systems cannot satisfy under dynamic environmental variability.
method: Quetzal combines a hardware power-measurement circuit with a two-part software runtime. The energy-aware scheduler selects jobs by minimizing end-to-end latency including projected energy recharging time, not just execution time. The runtime uses queueing-theory models to predict whether the selected job will cause an input buffer overflow before it completes; if overflow is imminent, it degrades the scheduled job (e.g., reduces quality or shortens duration) to lower processing latency and prevent buffer saturation. The hardware circuit is simple and system-agnostic, providing real-time power readings to the scheduler.
key_novelty: Integration of queueing-theory-based IBO prediction with energy-recharge-aware scheduling and job degradation, enabled by a lightweight hardware power measurement circuit, to dynamically prevent input buffer overflow on energy-harvesting devices.
contributions: Energy-aware scheduler that minimizes end-to-end latency by accounting for energy recharging time in job selection.
Runtime IBO prediction using queueing theory to proactively detect impending buffer overflows.
Job degradation mechanism that reduces processing load when overflow is imminent.
Reduction of missed events due to IBO by up to 4.2x versus baseline schedulers.

metrics.other: Up to 4.2x reduction in events missed due to input buffer overflow vs. baselines

baselines: several baseline energy-harvesting schedulers (unspecified in abstract)
limitations: Not discussed; the queueing-theory model assumes stationary statistics that may not hold under highly bursty or adversarial event patterns.
primary_theme: Energy-aware scheduling with IBO prevention for energy-harvesting IoT devices
